storage: Keep in an airtight tin or zip-lock pouch at room temperature away from damp; use within 2 to 3 weeks of opening, and re-crisp on a dry pan for a minute if it softens.
looksLike: A crunchy golden-yellow mix of deep-fried gram-flour (besan) pieces: thin and thick sev, gathiya, boondi, often with peanuts, fried dal, curry leaves and a dusting of chilli and salt. Mumbai "misal farsan" is a mostly sev-and-gathiya mix.
howToPick: Look for a sealed, puffed pouch (nitrogen-flushed), crisp pieces, and a fresh fried smell. Avoid a stale, oily or rancid smell, soft or chewy pieces, or a torn pack.
shelfLife: About 3 to 6 months sealed per typical pack labels (general guidance; not taken from a source in this run); eat within 2 to 3 weeks once opened.
substitutes: Plain thick sev (nylon or ratlami sev)
Crushed roasted peanuts or farali mixture

usedIn.raw: 25 g per serving (¼ cup), sprinkled on top of the misal
